mobile.firebase: Project qci-samar (763992459108), shared with the assessor app. Apps org.qcin.samar.applicant{,.staging,.development} on ANDROID + IOS. Configs committed: android/app/google-services.json (this app's three variants only) and ios/qciapplicantapp/firebase/GoogleService-Info-{Production,Staging,Development}.plist, selected at build time by prebuild.js. Crashlytics only — no other Firebase product is wired.
mobile.security: Security-grade tier (react-native.md): SecurityGuard.kt (Kotlin baseline + RootBeer, fail-closed) enforced from MainApplication.onCreate and MainActivity.onResume, Talsec, WebView debugging off, iOS anti-debug/jailbreak/Frida layer, TrustKit + network_security_config pinning on the ISRG roots. GUARD: SecurityGuard's RELEASE_CERT_SHA256/PLAY_CERT_SHA256 are UNSET until the fresh keystores exist (D-009) — while unset the SIGNATURE check is skipped (root/tamper detection still enforces). Filling them is a pre-submission gate. Never derive these at runtime: a re-signed APK satisfies its own derived hash.

diagnostics.crashes: Crashlytics via @react-native-firebase/crashlytics, consumed by Logger.recordError (src/utils/logger.js). NOT alerted on — crashes land in the console and nobody is paged.

healthCheckPaths.samar-api: https://samar-staging1.qci.org.in/api/health (the API this client depends on; the app itself has no probeable endpoint)

gaps: Crashlytics collects crashes but nothing alerts on them — deliberate (see $comment), not an oversight.
No force-update check (react-native.md `versionCheck.js`) — there is no way to push pilot users off a build, which D-007 step 5 (the production re-release) depends on.
No ErrorBoundary at the navigation root (react-native.md [Global]) — a render crash is a white screen in release, with no non-fatal recorded.

Force-update (useVersionCheck) only runs in Production and needs a published listing to compare against — untestable until the fresh listing is live, and it is what D-007's production re-release depends on.
monitoring.$comment: Alerting is DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED for this estate (Navneet, 20-Aug-2026) — pre-production, D-007 pilot. Crashlytics collects; nothing pages anyone, by choice. Revisit at production provisioning.

guards: BEFORE THE FIRST STORE SUBMISSION read docs/40-release/store-release.md section 6 (Launch-day notes) — it carries the things that are wrong-by-default months later, not just the happy path.

TLS pins: RE-VERIFY THE LIVE CHAIN before shipping, never trust the pin set as written. On 20-Aug-2026 Let's Encrypt served leaf -> YE1/YE2 -> ISRG Root YE -> ISRG Root X2, so we pin THREE roots (X1, X2, Root YE). X2 sits at the END of that chain and stops matching once Root YE reaches device trust stores — an X1/X2-only pin set then validates nothing, unfixable server-side, needs a store release. Pins live in android/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml and ios/qciapplicantapp/AppDelegate.swift (NOT appsettings).

SecurityGuard.kt PLAY_CERT_SHA256 is UNSET and the signature check is therefore SKIPPED. It cannot be filled before the Play listing exists (Play App Signing generates that key, and it re-signs distributed builds — enforcing with only our upload hash makes every Play install kill itself). Filling it is the last pre-submission gate.

SecurityGuard.isHardenedBuild() gates the KILL on FLAVOR == 'production', not on !BuildConfig.DEBUG. That looks like an oversight and is not: assembleStagingRelease/assembleDevelopmentRelease are release builds, and every Android emulator reports test-keys, SELinux permissive and ro.debuggable — the 'simplification' kills a tester's staging APK on launch. Same for enforceThrottled() on the network interceptor.
